run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }` query and tell me how many hits come back. If that returns zero, find the right field for log level and re-run the query.

report.summary: The query `term: {level: "ERROR"}` on index app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d returned 0 hits. The index has no `level` field: its mapping contains only @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword), so the requested field name does not exist there. Re-running the same term query on the correct field, `severity`, returned 10 hits, all with service=checkout-275. Over the tool-applied window 2026-11-23T17:08:46Z–2026-11-23T18:08:46Z (the search tool always filters on @timestamp, here the hour ending at the authorized window end), the index matched 30 documents with severity buckets INFO 15, ERROR 10, WARN 5, so the 10 ERROR hits are consistent with the full severity distribution in that hour. The sampled ERROR documents carry messages of the form 'DB connection refused N' from checkout-275 at 18:05:08–18:05:10Z; the underlying cause of those log lines was not investigated in this Run, and this answer is a count, not an impact assessment.

claims.text: The query {"term": {"level": "ERROR"}} against app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d returned 0 hits (total.value 0, relation eq) over the tool-applied @timestamp window 2026-11-23T17:08:46Z to 2026-11-23T18:08:46Z.

The mapping of index app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d defines only these fields: @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword), severity (keyword); there is no `level` field, which explains the zero result for term level:ERROR.

Re-running the term query on the correct field, {"term": {"severity": "ERROR"}}, returned 10 hits (total.value 10, relation eq) in the same window; the service aggregation shows all 10 in the single bucket service=checkout-275 and the severity aggregation shows the single bucket severity=ERROR with doc_count 10.

Unfiltered over the same window, app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d matched 30 documents with severity buckets INFO 15, ERROR 10 and WARN 5 (sum_other_doc_count 0), so ERROR accounts for 10 of 30 documents in that hour.

Sampled ERROR documents are service=checkout-275 with messages 'DB connection refused 8', 'DB connection refused 9' and 'DB connection refused 10' at 2026-11-23T18:05:08Z, 18:05:09Z and 18:05:10Z; 10 ERROR documents matched and only 3 were shown, so the view is marked incomplete.
The index app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d exists, is open and green, and holds 30 documents (7.3kb) at the moment of the query.

The 10 ERROR hits are concentrated at 18:05:01Z–18:05:10Z per source_start_at/source_end_at, and the sampled document view showed only 3 of the 10 matching documents (incomplete view), so the full set of ERROR messages and their exact time span were not read.
Whether term severity:ERROR returns the same count over other periods of the authorized window was not tested; no time-series or range breakdown was run.
The cause of the 'DB connection refused' messages logged by checkout-275 was not investigated; no database dependency state, pod status/events or trace evidence was examined in this Run.
next_steps: If a time-series view is needed, repeat the severity:ERROR count with explicit start_time/end_time sub-windows inside the authorized window rather than relying on the default one-hour filter.
If the checkout-275 'DB connection refused' errors matter operationally, correlate them against the checkout service's traces and the database dependency's pod status and events.
